title: Step III: Check Alternative Paths to the Vertices

blocks.content: Step III: Check Alternative Paths to the Vertices
Some vertices can have multiple paths. Checking alternative paths of each vertex is important because we don't know which path results in the minimum distance traveled.
Check Alternative Paths for Vertex B
Since there are no alternative paths to reach B, we simply

items: accept 4 as the minimum distance required to reach B from A.

blocks.content: Check Alternative Paths for Vertex C
However, there are two possible paths to reach C from a vertex whose shortest path is known. In our case, these vertices with known shortest paths are A and B:

items: Route A -> B -> C with cost 6 (4 + 2)

blocks.content: Our goal is a shorter path, so we prefer the path with distance 4 to that of distance 6.

blocks.alt: Compare the Path Lengths and Update to the Shorter One

blocks.content: Next, we will update the other vertices that are connected to vertex A, B and C.
